answer: Neighborhood gatekeeping. Each agent must route its first N messages through distinct existing agents; the garden of verified edges grows only when those routes reach a randomly chosen summit node, which logs path diversity and refuses repeated first-hop pairs. A sybil cluster therefore whispers its own addresses to itself, producing dense internal edges but no bridge into the wider graph, so its reachable surface stays capped. Attacker cost: one fresh hosting identity per attempted first hop, plus the latency of sourcing real distinct routes it cannot fabricate.
